title: Kim leads ‘V-Day’ events as North Korea highlights Chinese help in Korean War - nknews.org
content:
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un attended events Monday marking the 73rd anniversary of the “victory in the Fatherland Liberation War” over the U.S., according to state media, emphasizing China’s assistance in the war. The Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) reported Tuesday that the July 27 concert took place at the Pyongyang Indoor Stadium, followed by a small-scale military parade outside the venue to celebrate the so-called victory in the 1950-53 Korean War. The concert included a video segment showing Kim and Chinese leader Xi Jinping’s recent meeting in Pyongyangand clips of Chinese troops during the war. Chinese Ambassador North Korean leader Kim Jong Un attended events Monday marking the 73rd anniversary of the “victory in the Fatherland Liberation War” over the U.S., according to state media, emphasizing China’s assistance in the war. The Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) reported Tuesday that the July 27 concert took place at the Pyongyang Indoor Stadium, followed by a small-scale military parade outside the venue to celebrate the so-called victory in the 1950-53 Korean War. The concert included a video segment showing Kim and Chinese leader Xi Jinping’s recent meeting in Pyongyang and clips of Chinese troops during the war. Chinese Ambassador to the DPRK Wang Yajun and Russian Chargé d’Affaires Vladimir Topekha were invited as special guests. KCNA said attendees were “deeply touched” by the “matchless self-sacrificing spirit, heroism and brilliant feats of excellent sons and daughters of the Chinese people who shared life and death” and fought “shoulder to shoulder” with North Koreans in the war. China entered the Korean War in Oct. 1950, pushing U.S.-led forces back from their advance toward the Chinese border and ultimately stabilizing the front near the 38th parallel. North Korean founding leader Kim Il Sung invaded the South four months earlier in an attempt to unify the peninsula under his rule. Major hostilities were halted on July 27, 1953, with the signing of the Armistice Agreement by the DPRK, China and the U.S.-led U.N. Command. North Korean propaganda continues to call the July 27 holiday the “Day of Victory” while falsely claiming it was a righteous war to repel an invasion by South Korea and the U.S. Monday’s performances were meant as a message of the “DPRK people’s eternal thanks to the brave fighters of the Chinese People’s Volunteers,” KCNA reported, calling the war a joint mission of “resisting America.” “The DPRK-China friendship, based on the shared ideal and militant fraternity, will be immortal along with the history of the great war victory,” it added. Kim also visited the Cemetery of the Fallen Soldiers of the Chinese People’s Volunteers (CPV) on Sunday to pay his respects to Chinese soldiers. He visited the cemetery in October and around the July 27 holiday in 2023 as well, when state media presented a similarly high emphasis on Chinese assistance to mark the 70th anniversary. The focus on China was more subdued at anniversary events in the last two years, but Beijing and Pyongyang have recently appeared to seek closer relations again after the DPRK’s pandemic-era policies slowed down business ties and ended Chinese tourism. State media characterized the celebratory events as an “ideological and mental nutrient” for the North Korean people and military, encouraging patriotism and loyalty to the state. Kim attended the concert with his wife Ri Sol Ju and his young daughter. State TV cameras focused closely on the leader and his daughter during its coverage, as has become standard in recent years, but the KCNA text report did not mention his family’s presence. They didn’t appear at the parade with Kim, who appeared on the viewing platform with current and retired generals, as well as elderly war veterans who should now be in their late 80s and 90s. Kim did not make a speech at this year’s events after doing so at July 27 celebrations in years past. Defense minister No Kwang Chol delivered brief remarks at what KCNA called the “ceremonial parade of the columns symbolic of the units who fought in the Fatherland Liberation War.” He vowed to remain vigilant against “forces that are threatening at every moment,” but did not  include pointed messages at the U.S. and ROK. The parade featured around a dozen block formations, each with 160 young soldiers wearing Korean War-era uniforms and representing divisions named after famous generals and celebrated battles like the “liberation” of Seoul. KCNA praised soldiers who became “human bombs” in the war by carrying out suicide attacks, echoing North Korea’s active policy in the Ukraine war requiring soldiers to kill themselves to complete attacks and avoid capture. Symbolic units of horse-drawn carriages and motorcycles rounded out the historical procession, followed by three formations representing the current-era army, navy and air force to end the parade. Similar concerts and military marches took place at the Pyongyang Indoor Stadium on July 27 in 2024 and 2025 as well, with Kim skipping last year’s events. While North Korea is still engaged in a war alongside Russia against Ukraine, the holiday does not generally serve as a memorial day for all war casualties and Monday’s events appeared mostly focused on the Korean War.
